newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Menem's ex-wife protests over son's death.
newsitem.headline: Menem's ex-wife protests over son's death.

text.p: Former Argentine first lady Zulema Yoma, who accuses her ex-husband President Carlos Menem's government of a cover-up in their son's death in 1995, staged a sit-in protest on Wednesday at police headquarters.
Carlos Menem Jr. died in 1995 at the age of 26 when the helicopter he was piloting crashed. The original Air Force report said the crash was an accident.

Yoma alleges that her son's death was not an accident, but a political murder that was being covered up by security services. Various newspapers have carried alleged leaks of a police report on the case showing that the helicopter wreckage bore the traces of four bullet holes.
Yoma accused a judge investigating the case of delaying release of the report because it was politically sensitive.
The report is due to be issued on Thursday, but Yoma said she wanted it released immediately and vowed to stay at the police headquarters until Menem showed up.

"I am not going until the president comes," Yoma told reporters. "I can confirm the bullets...but I want the president of the nation, Carlitos Menem's dad, to come to police headquarters to find out for himself."
"I won't accept it being delayed for political reasons," she said.
The president's response was to send his lawyer, Ricardo Klass, who told reporters the release of the report was being delayed because it had to be studied by the judge first.
The Air Force's 1995 investigation reported that Carlos Menem Jr. was flying his chopper low along a highway when he hit a cable, killing himself and a friend flying with him.
The 67-year-old president was devastated by the death of his son. But he does not support Yoma's theory, calling it the product of a mother's grief.

Yoma, who divorced Menem after being thrown out of the palace in 1990, has ignored dismissals by senior officials that she is hysterical and has lobbied tirelessly against what she says is a murky plot involving politics and drugs.
She has had the body exhumed for a second autopsy and has managed to get the word "accident" removed from the file.

The former first lady's conspiracy theory is gradually gaining acceptance and even the public prosecutor in charge of the case, Amalia Sivori, told a newspaper this week that she was investigating "a possible double homicide."

Caught in the middle is Yoma and Menem's daughter Zulemita who has been Menem's acting first lady since the divorce. She joined her mother at police headquarters in an obvious state of distress, choking back tears as she told reporters:
"You have to understand Daddy's position, he is president. And Mummy has every right in the world to make her demands because she is the mother. I'm caught in the middle."
